title: As of November 9, 2026 morning, neither the Lok Sabha nor the Rajya Sabha had been formally prorogued, keeping open the possibility of convening an extended sitting of the existing session
author: PTI
content_html:
Parliament's Monsoon session has remained unprorogued for 88 days since both Houses were adjourned indefinitely on August 13, breaking the previous record of 87 days in 2008.

As of Monday (November 9, 2026) morning, neither the Lok Sabha nor the Rajya Sabha had been formally prorogued, keeping open the possibility of convening an extended sitting of the existing session.

The government's decision not to prorogue (formally end) the Monsoon session has kept alive speculation about the possibility of convening Parliament at short notice to consider the proposed constitutional amendment linked to the implementation of the Women's Reservation Bill, which seeks to increase the strength of the Lok Sabha from 543 seats to a maximum of 850 through delimitation.

An extended or special sitting of Parliament within the same session requires a minimum notice of two days, whereas convening a fresh session requires at least 14 days' notice.

This has added significance as a similar Constitution Amendment Bill had failed to secure the required numbers in the Lok Sabha during a special sitting of the Budget session on April 17.

The Constitution does not prescribe any specific time frame within which a House must be prorogued after being adjourned sine die (for an indefinite period).

The mere fact that a House remains unprorogued for an extended period does not, by itself, amount to any constitutional or procedural impropriety.

According to records, Parliament had remained unprorogued for 87 days in 2008, 76 days in 1987, 54 days in 1989, 49 days each in 2006 and 2013, and 41 days in 1963.

In 2008, the Lok Sabha met for two days, July 21 and 22, to discuss the no-confidence motion against the then UPA government. The House was subsequently kept unprorogued, reconvened on October 17 and was adjourned on October 24 to meet again on December 10.

title: ‘Dimagi Naxals’ instigating people against Constitution: PM Modi as Maoists eliminated
author: PTI
content_html:
Targeting political opponents, Prime Minister Narendra Modi on Sunday (November 8, 2026) said armed Maoists had been eliminated, but “dimagi Naxals” (ideological supporters) had infiltrated several political parties and organisations and were instigating people against the Constitution and democracy.

“We must identify and defeat such elements and secure the country,” Mr. Modi said, while celebrating Deepavali with security personnel at a Central Reserve Police Force (CRPF) camp in Bastar, Chhattisgarh, continuing his tradition of spending the festival with the men and women in uniform. The government declared the country free of Naxalism on March 31, 2026.

“Amid the successes, we must remember one more thing. Naxalites have been eliminated, but the threat is not over yet. Armed Naxalites have disappeared from the forests, but ‘dimagi Naxals’ have taken control of several organisations,” he said.

“Even today, they are instigating people against the country’s Constitution and democracy. They have infiltrated several political parties and different organisations. We must identify and defeat them and secure the country,” he added. The government, he said, took decisions that “dealt very big blows to the funding of Naxals and secessionists”.

On Independence Day in August 2026, Mr. Modi had also referred to “dimagi Naxals”, saying the country had succeeded in removing armed Naxalism but its ideological supporters were seeking opportunities to promote violence.

Recalling the fight against Naxalism in Bastar, Mr. Modi said it had not been easy, as at one point over 230 districts across nearly 20 States were affected by Left-Wing Extremism. After sunset, life would come to a standstill, thousands of villages and crores of people were affected, and there were around 2,000 Naxalite attacks annually, he said.

“This land had become soaked in the blood of our brave personnel, but not a single sigh of grief was heard from any of the ‘naamdaar’ (powerful people) living in palaces. Not a single tear rolled down their eyes. Such attacks continued to take place somewhere or the other almost every day,” he said, targeting previous governments. Between 2004 and 2013, more security personnel were killed every year than the number of Naxalites eliminated, he said.

“Unfortunately, the governments of that time treated Naxalism as an incurable disease and left it unaddressed. No country can function with such an approach towards its enemies... The lack of political will that the country faced was addressed in 2014, when you gave this Pradhan Sevak the opportunity to serve Mother India,” he said.

The morale of security forces began changing after 2014, Mr. Modi said, adding that for the first time in 47 years, not a single CRPF personnel lost his life while on duty over the past year. “This is a victory of the country’s right policies and strong political will. This is a victory of your valour, courage and restraint,” he said.

Diwali is sweeter with those who protect us! #Bastar #NaxalFreeIndia https://t.co/7Ywie7uTt4

— Narendra Modi (@narendramodi) November 8, 2026

The Prime Minister said the government had taken tough decisions to strengthen national security, including measures not widely known.

“These decisions and efforts dealt a major blow to the funding networks of Naxalites and secessionists. The fake currency nexus was destroyed. This not only broke their financial backbone but also choked their entire supply lines. As a result, the supply of weapons was stopped, and the recruitment of Naxalites was curbed,” he said.

Mr. Modi alleged that previous governments tied the hands of security forces during ground operations and denied them the freedom to retaliate effectively against Maoist attacks. “We gave security forces the freedom to take every necessary decision. We also worked to stop the support that Left-Wing Extremism received from certain people within the government and the system,” he said.

The government’s objective, he said, was to ensure that no mother lost her child, no family was pushed into devastation, no child took up arms, and no youth’s future was destroyed. “Without publicity or showmanship, we worked with sensitivity and broke the backbone of Maoist terrorists. We transformed the lives of people in Naxal-affected areas through a spirit of service, which led those suffering from Naxalism to stand firmly with the government and security forces,” he said.

Over the past 12 years, the country had not only won the battle against Naxalism and secessionists, but also achieved a major victory in its fight against poverty, Mr. Modi said, citing a World Bank report that 50 crore people had come out of extreme poverty in India. “What decades of ‘garibi hatao’ slogans could not achieve, the country accomplished in just 12 years,” he said.

He said India had the capability to fulfil its resolutions, citing the abrogation of Article 370, the construction of household toilets, and the expansion of vaccination coverage. “When we speak of eliminating poverty, building a drug-free India, creating a developed India and making India self-reliant, the country will achieve these goals as well,” he added.

title: Rape-murder accused killed in police encounter; fourth case in West Bengal since BJP came to power
author: Senjuti Sengupta
content_html:
A prime accused in the rape and murder of a minor in West Bengal’s Raiganj was shot dead by the police when he tried to flee to Bihar. This is the fourth such encounter in the State in the last four months since the Bharatiya Janata Party (BJP) government came to power.

According to police officials, the accused, Dilip Roy, had been fleeing since the mutilated body of the 13-year-old minor was recovered on Thursday (November 5, 2026). At around 3:30 a.m. on Monday (November 9, 2026), in the early hours, police went to arrest him in the Gauri village area, from where he was trying to cross into Bihar.

Soon the police reached the spot, he opened fire at the cops. Dilip was killed in a retaliatory firing during the incident, said police. 

He was rushed to a nearby hospital, where he was declared dead. Later, the body was sent for an autopsy. 

Police said that the minor victim went missing on Tuesday (November 3, 2026). Later, her mutilated body was recovered from the Kulik Wildlife Sanctuary on Thursday (Novemeber 5, 2026). After a preliminary investigation, a case of rape and murder was lodged at the Raiganj police station by her parents, following which the police began searching for the accused involved in the case, including Dilip Roy.

Reacting to the development, the panchayat Minister Dilip Ghosh said that police will have to take such action if anyone violates the laws.

“Such crimes will not be spared. If everyone follows the law and order, nothing will happen. But police have a duty to act if accused individuals attempt to evade the law or escape,” he said. 

Monday’s development comes only 13 days after two more encounters took place on October 28 at only twelve hours apart.

Samaul Sheikh, who was a key accused in the murder of BJP worker Sujit Mondal on August 28, was shot dead in a gunfight with police in Murshidabad at around 3 p.m. on Tuesday (October 27, 2026). About 12 hours ago, Prahlad Das, accused of raping and murdering a minor girl in North 24 Parganas’ Gaighata, was shot dead in an encounter at around 3.30 a.m.

Earlier, on July 8, a similar encounter took place in the South 24 Parganas Baruipur area, when police took Prabhas Mondal, the prime accused in the rape and murder of a minor girl, to reconstruct the crime scene.

The area had been tense since July 5, when the body of the 12-year-old girl was recovered from a pond after she was allegedly raped and murdered.

On November 3, the Chief Minister Suvendu Adhikari warned the criminals that they will not be spared if anyone causes any harm to the women in the State. 

“You all are seeing what is happening when someone lays hands on our mothers and sisters,” CM Adhikari had said on November 3.

title: Air of Deepavali celebrations lingers in Hyderabad with AQI remaining at hazardous levels
author: Serish Nanisetti
content_html:
Hyderabad woke up to a grey smoggy morning on Monday (November 9, 2026) a day after a Big Bang Deepavali celebration that went on till 3 a.m. in the morning in many central localities like Banjara Hills, Srinagar Colony, Panjagutta, S.R. Nagar, Ameerpet and Somajiguda. 

The air quality in Hyderabad deteriorated in the night itself with particulate matter 2.5 reaching 392 micrograms per cubic meter (μg/m³) at 9.30 p.m. and the Air Quality Index averaged 509. At the same time, Ravi Colony near Masjid Banda logged 995 AQI as crackers went off one after the other.

The data was sourced from publicly available pollution monitors as the Telangana Pollution Control Board monitors were out of order as the air pollution was rising. By 10 p.m. the TSPCB’s University of Hyderabad monitoring station was offline.

The air had a metallic sulphurous smell in many areas as the crackers went off one after the other. “For the first time in Hyderabad, I’m experiencing air pollution this bad. My eyes are burning, the air is thick with the stench of burnt chemicals and gunpowder, and breathing itself feels uncomfortable. It’s only 10 PM. The entire colony is still out, relentlessly bursting crackers. The roads are covered in the remains of firecrackers, and this photograph captures barely a fraction of the mess,” wrote one social media user.

The high AQI recordings were almost evenly spread through the city as a 20 degree celsius wind blew from the north-eastern direction.

The air pollution hit a peak at 9.30 p.m. before slowly dropping down through the night. At 11.30 p.m. when the average AQI in Hyderabad was 442, Serilingampally recorded a high of 666. 

By morning it still remained hazardous at 178 AQI with PM 10 reaching 113 μg/m³.

title: NDA seals YSRCP’s fate in rural local body polls by winning 499 ZPTC and 5,861 MPTC seats
author: V. Raghavendra
content_html:
The NDA partners TDP, Jana Sena Party (JSP) and BJP sealed the YSR Congress Party (YSRCP)’s fate in the elections to 582 Zilla Parishad Territorial Constituencies (ZPTCs) by winning 499 (TDP 406, JSP 73 and BJP 20) seats confining the YSRCP to 76 seats.

In the elections to 7,768 Mandal Parishad Territorial Constituencies (MPTCs), TDP won 4,806, JSP 938 and BJP 117 (total 5,861). YSRCP won 1,711 MPTCs, CPI (M) 15, Congress 9 and Bhajuan Samaj Party 3.

Gram Panchayat polls from Nov. 26

Meanwhile, the State Election Commission set the stage for elections to Gram Panchayats in three phases i.e on November 26 and 29 and December 2, for which the Commission will issue notifications on November 13, 16 and 19.

The SEC announced the lifting of the Model Code of Conduct (MCC) in 100 Urban Local Bodies (Municipal Corporations and Municipalities) following the completion of elections to them. However, the MCC is in force in the rural areas where elections are due on the given dates.
